item.text: {"text":"Search found related work, but no verified 2023–2026 match combining a lightweight, randomly initialized title/description encoder with GRU4Rec under the stated restrictions. [Recformer (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13731) learns text-based item and sequence representations, reporting benefits in low-resource and cold-start settings; its Transformer backbone and pretraining pipeline make it unsuitable as a direct implementation here. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) incorporates titles, descriptions and reviews using BERT, so it also differs from the allowed inputs and initialization. An older, closer methodological precedent, [Ask the GRU (2016)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.02116), trains a GRU text encoder end-to-end for collaborative filtering, with auxiliary metadata prediction; it does not establish effectiveness for this sequential benchmark.\n\nA plausible experiment—not a literature-verified improvement—is a shared, randomly initialized token embedding plus mean pooling or a small CNN over available titles/descriptions, projected and jointly combined with item-ID embeddings inside the existing GRU model. Train the text encoder through the same next-item objective and use the resulting item representation consistently for history encoding and candidate scoring, retaining one network/checkpoint per category. Shared tokens could transfer interaction supervision between items; a CNN could additionally capture local phrases. Whether these relationships improve sparse-item recommendations remains unverified: noisy descriptions, weak token supervision and generic vocabulary could erase the benefit. Select using the fixed macro validation HR@10; retain final-nonpadding readout and matching predictor serialization."}
